subject: Aligning product walkthrough to finance sprint and exec travel
messages:
From: Ronan Blake <ronan@stratecon.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinanceOps <financeops@stratecon.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick ask — walkthrough timing for pilot

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the primer last week. We’re keen to get a short hands-on walkthrough (30–45 min) that focuses on inference economics and routing policies — our procurement and FinOps folks want to understand the timing implications before we land on budget.

One wrinkle: our CFO is on a roadshow from 22–26 Mar and the finance team has a sprint on the 24th that will lock prioritization for Q2 spend. If possible, could we either move the session earlier (week of 15th) or pick a follow-up window the first week after the sprint (starting 29th)? We don’t want to drag this past their commit window but also need exec visibility.

Attached is a short list of items they care about. Happy to be flexible.

—Ronan

Attachments: purchase-timing-overview.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ronan Blake <ronan@stratecon.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick ask — walkthrough timing for pilot

Hi Ronan — thanks for the heads-up and for sharing the spreadsheet.

Karthik / Laura: FYI — Stratecon needs the walkthrough scoped to finance timing and will prefer either this week or the week of Mar 29 once the sprint closes. Their CFO travel (22–26) makes the 22nd–26th impossible for exec-level attendance.

Proposed options:
- Option A: Short technical+economics walkthrough on Thu 18 Mar, 30 minutes (we record and follow with a 1-hr deep-dive for FinOps on 29 Mar if needed)
- Option B: Keep the planned 30-min slot the week of 29 Mar and schedule a separate procurement Q&A for 30–45 minutes (FinOps + Procurement) on 31 Mar

We should try A if we can line up Anya from product for the economics section and surface the agenda. If not, go with B to ensure the FinOps eyes are on the session with Procurement present.

I’ve attached a one-pager agenda you can share. If you want, I’ll also draft a short mutual action plan to lock the deliverables and decision gates.

Thanks — Evelyn

Attachments: MVP-walkthrough-agenda.pdf (PDF, 18KB)
From: Ronan Blake <ronan@stratecon.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick ask — walkthrough timing for pilot

> Hi Ronan — thanks for the heads-up and for sharing the spreadsheet.
> 
> Karthik / Laura: FYI — Stratecon needs the walkthrough scoped to finance timing and will prefer either this week or the week of Mar 29 once the sprint closes. Their CFO travel (22–26) makes the 22nd–26th impossible for exec-level attendance.

> - Option B: Keep the planned 30-min slot the week of 29 Mar and schedule a separate procurement Q&A for 30–45 minutes (FinOps + Procurement) on 31 Mar
>

Thanks — Evelyn

Evelyn — Option A works for our managers, but Procurement has requested Procurement Lead (Liam) be present for any pricing/term discussion and he’s only available on 31 Mar. Given the finance sprint kicks off on the 24th and their lock happens on the 26th, I worry a short 18 Mar session without Liam will create extra churn.

Can we do this: run a concise 18 Mar demo (30 min) strictly focused on product capability and latency/cost examples, explicitly exclude pricing/contract talk, and schedule the pricing + procurement Q&A for Wed 31 Mar? If that works for your side, we’ll block internal calendars accordingly.

We’ll be flexible on times — morning CET preferred.

Best,
Ronan
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ronan Blake <ronan@stratecon.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick ask — walkthrough timing for pilot

Thanks, Ronan — that split approach makes sense and prevents the procurement gating from delaying product visibility. Plan below:

1) Thu 18 Mar, 09:30–10:00 CET — Product capability & economics demo (no pricing/contract content). Presenters: Evelyn (product overview), Karthik (inference economics). We’ll record and circulate the clip and short notes.

2) Wed 31 Mar, 10:00–10:45 CET — Procurement & pricing Q&A (Liam from Stratecon, Laura from Redwood legal will attend). Agenda: pricing bands, milestone-based invoices, PO timing, and procurement checklist.

Action items: 
- Evelyn: finalize 18 Mar slide deck and recording plan (deliver by 17 Mar EOD) — DONE (see attached agenda)
- Karthik: prepare 5–7 min cost examples for typical batch/stream workloads — IN PROGRESS
- Laura: draft a short procurement checklist and a sample SOW clause to speed PO review — IN PROGRESS

Ronan — I’ve shared the calendar invites (link below) and attached the agenda. If anything changes on your end because of the CFO travel, ping me and we’ll pivot. Looking forward to it.

Links: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=0a1b2c3d4e5f
